note: Adapted from Snyder's 1924 English account; the original is in English. Snyder re-examined only the female alate of Hagen's 1860 type and gave a comparative description, without redescribing the whole form; Hagen's original was not obtained. In the original comparison table the fumosus column is misaligned by OCR (header and figures on separate lines); apart from the left mandible length 0.6—0.7 mm explicitly given in the text, no other measurements from the table were used, to avoid attributing them to another species.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Distance between ocelli and eyes slightly less than the ocellus diameter; postclypeus twice as wide as long (key, item 5); body larger than in ater, mandibles longer, postclypeus more projecting than in ater, mandibles extending slightly beyond the labrum.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: As recorded by Snyder from the re-examined type specimen (female, M.C.Z. type no. 218, from Vera Cruz, Mexico): body larger than in ater, dark brown, mandibles longer; eyes projecting, prominent; postclypeus paler than the head, projecting and prominent, twice as wide as long, bilobed, more distinct than in ater; mandibles extending slightly beyond the labrum; distance between ocelli and eyes about equal to their diameter; fontanelle an indistinct spot at the base of the coronal suture, medially behind the ocelli, situated farther forward than in ater; coronal suture more distinct than in ater. Left mandible length 0.6—0.7 mm.
